questions.stem: A sprinter builds up a larger oxygen debt than a jogger covering the same distance. Why?

options.text: The sprinter uses less oxygen overall
The sprinter relies more on anaerobic respiration, producing more lactic acid
The jogger does not carry out any respiration
The sprinter breathes more during the run

questions.explanation: Sprinting is high-intensity exercise where oxygen supply cannot meet demand, so more anaerobic respiration occurs and more lactic acid accumulates. Jogging is lower intensity, allowing aerobic respiration to dominate.
